course_description:
This course offers students the opportunity to undertake an internship with a public or private art institution within Australia or internationally; or complete a major independent research project.

For those interested in internships, students must apply directly to the institutions and have formal acceptance prior to the commencement of the course. The course convener must also grant school approval for the internship to count toward the course prior to commencing the course and internship (see suitability guidelines and further information here ).

The research stream requires students to undertake an individual and self-guided research project, with guidance from a supervisor. Research Topics are decided in consultation with a staff member whose expertise aligns with student’s independent research area. Students are encouraged to focus on institutional art archives and art collections and require a GPA of 5.0 or above to undertake this course. The independent research project application form is available here .

Both internship and research stream students are required to engage an academic supervisor as part of their participation in the course. Once a placement

The independent research option of this course is designed for students who are considering doing Honours in art history and who have the opportunity to complete a focused research project in the field of art history. Research projects can involve examination of scholarly archives in public institutions or other approved art institutions. Students must secure approval from a suitable supervisor prior to enrolment.

The internship option is designed to help students gain visual arts industry experience and to gain understanding of the professional applications of art history study. Students must obtain a place in a formal internship program at a public art institution prior to enrolment. Once they have secured this internship they then seek approval from an art history lecturer who will supervise the academic requirements of the course.ﾠ

course_aims:
The aim of this course is to provide advanced art history students with an opportunity to conduct focused study in art history by way of archival research, or through a formal internship experience.ﾠ

The requirements for students to work with either a public art archive or to conduct an internship at a public art museum are designed to enhance relations between the study of art history and the visual arts industry.ﾠ

Students who complete the course will gain experience in working off-campus within the visual arts industry and develop scholarly skills in the research and presentation of art.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand some of the work practices of the visual arts industry
Conduct independent research on a focused topic in the discipline of art history
Write an extended essay or report regarding an area of research or work practice in art history and/or the visual arts industry
